author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
review: 'The Great Gatsby' by F. Scott Fitzgerald is a timeless masterpiece that delves into the decadence and disillusionment of the Jazz Age. Set in the Roaring Twenties, the novel unveils the enigmatic Jay Gatsby's extravagant parties.

author: Harper Lee
review: Harper Lee's 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is a profound coming-of-age story that explores racial injustice and moral growth in the American South through the innocent eyes of young Scout Finch.

author: George Orwell
review: George Orwell's dystopian masterpiece '1984' presents a chilling vision of a totalitarian future where Big Brother monitors every thought, examining themes of censorship and psychological control.

author: Jane Austen
review: A classic romance novel that cleverly critiques the social class and marriage expectations of 19th-century England through the fiery dynamic between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy.

author: J.D. Salinger
review: This iconic novel captures teenage alienation and angst through Holden Caulfield's cynical yet vulnerable narrative as he wanders New York City after being expelled from prep school.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: An enchanting fantasy adventure following Bilbo Baggins as he leaves his peaceful home to embark on an epic quest to reclaim the lost Dwarf Kingdom of Erebor from the dragon Smaug.

author: Ray Bradbury
review: Ray Bradbury's thought-provoking story depicts a future American society where books are outlawed and 'firemen' burn any that are found, raising critical questions about mass media.

author: Charlotte Brontë
review: A powerful gothic romance following the emotional and spiritual journey of an orphaned woman who overcomes hardship to find independence and love at Thornfield Hall.

author: George Orwell
review: A satirical allegorical novella that reflects the events leading up to the Russian Revolution of 1917, showing how revolutionary ideals can be corrupted by power and greed.

author: Aldous Huxley
review: Set in a technologically advanced future where humans are genetically engineered and conditioned, this novel explores the loss of individuality and truth in exchange for forced happiness.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: An inspirational fable about an Andalusian shepherd boy named Santiago who travels from his homeland in Spain to the Egyptian desert in search of a treasure buried near the Pyramids.

author: William Golding
review: A gripping novel about a group of British schoolboys stranded on an uninhabited island whose attempt to govern themselves descends into savagery and instinctual chaos.

author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
review: A psychological drama focused on the mental anguish and moral dilemmas of Rodion Raskolnikov, an impoverished ex-student in Saint Petersburg who formulates a plan to kill an unscrupulous pawnbroker.

author: Oscar Wilde
review: Oscar Wilde's philosophical novel revolves around a portrait painted of Dorian Gray. As Gray remains youthful, his portrait ages and records every sin he commits.

author: Gabriel García Márquez
review: A landmark magical realism novel recounting the multi-generational story of the Buendía family, whose patriarch founded the mythical town of Macondo in Colombia.
